title: Introduce KMS rotation-escrow, canonical audit forwarder, and temporal RBAC delegation proxy
author: Aisha Kapoor
release_notes:
- Add KMS Rotation Escrow service to coordinate deterministic key rotation across regions while preserving residency constraints.
- Add Canonical Audit Forwarder that normalizes audit envelopes and attaches rotation provenance metadata.
- Add Temporal RBAC Delegation Proxy to support short-lived operator delegations with audit stamping and TTL enforcement.
description:
Title: Introduce KMS rotation-escrow, canonical audit forwarder, and temporal RBAC delegation proxy

Context and motivation: We need a coordinated, auditable approach to rotate customer CMKs across multi-region deployments without violating data residency assertions. Previous incidents (see SUP-987) highlighted gaps: out-of-band key rotation sequences producing mismatched audit provenance and operator sessions that persisted longer than intended. This change introduces three cooperating subsystems: (1) KMS Rotation Escrow service (rotation escrow), (2) Canonical Audit Forwarder (audit-canon), and (3) Temporal RBAC Delegation Proxy (delegation-ttl). The goal is to make rotations deterministic, auditable, and safe for operator delegation scenarios.

Goals (checklist):
- [x] Implement rotation escrow broker and API to coordinate rotation phases between primary and fallback providers.
- [x] Persist rotation metadata and rotation-proof (signed rotation envelope) to audit store.
- [x] Add audit canonicalizer that normalizes envelopes and attaches rotation-proof references for downstream compliance pipelines.
- [x] Introduce RBAC proxy that issues time-limited delegation tokens bound to rotation envelopes and target geozone.
- [x] Unit + integration tests for critical flows (rotation -> audit -> delegation).
- [x] Update docs and operator runbook with safe rollback steps.

Design summary and key behaviors: rotation-escrow: a lightweight coordinator (stateless API with short-lived persistent objects) that accepts a proposed rotation plan, stores an encrypted rotation-envelope (encrypted under the customer's escrow-wrapping key) and issues a rotation-proof token once the plan is applied by all participating KMS adapters. The escrow object stores region assertions so consumers can enforce residency rules. The escrow service never holds plaintext key material; it stores the wrapped envelope and a small provenance record signed by the service's signing key.

audit-canon: a pipeline component that consumes audit envelopes from the runtime, canonicalizes field names across providers, validates rotation-proof tokens against the escrow service, and emits normalized records with provenance metadata (rotation_id, escrow_signer, applied_regions). This enables downstream compliance queries like: "which rotation applied to tenant X during window Y and which operator delegations were active?"

delegation-ttl: a transparent proxy sitting in front of operator-facing endpoints that issues ephemeral delegation tokens (TTL default 15 minutes) and stamps the delegation with the rotation_id it was granted against. Delegation tokens are constrained by region claims and cannot be used to perform rotations themselves unless explicitly allowed in a rotation plan. The proxy includes rate-limits and an audit hooks integration to ensure every delegation issuance is captured in canonical audit records.

Small snippet (delegation binding check, simplified):
if delegation.TTL > maxTTL || !delegation.RegionClaim.ValidFor(rotation.AppliedRegions) {
    return errors.New("delegation exceeds allowed scope")
}

Migration notes: Added escrow table (rotation_envelopes) with columns: rotation_id, tenant_id, wrapped_envelope (bytea), applied_regions (jsonb), state, created_at, signed_proof. See infra/db/migrations/20251112_add_rotation_escrow.sql for migration details and a safety guard to only run in clusters where "rotation_escrow_enabled" feature flag is set.

Testing and CI: Initial CI run flagged a flaky integration test (audit-canon Kafka consumer timeout) which was fixed by increasing the test harness consumer group timeout and swapping to the local test topic; CI reruns subsequently passed. Current CI: all unit tests + integration suite + linter pass on main matrix (linux/go1.20, linux/go1.22).

Review conversation (high-level timeline):
- Miguel Santos (reviewer): "Large design surface — please add explicit threat model entries for escrow key-wrapping compromise and operator delegation misuse. Also add an E2E test that simulates a partial rotation failure and ensures we can roll back state."
- Author (Aisha): "Added threat model doc section and new e2e test (rotation-partial-failure) that simulates a mid-apply outage; escrow now records state transitions and exposes a rollback endpoint guarded by an operator workflow."
- Priya Nair (reviewer): "Can we ensure the escrow signer key rotates and that old proofs remain verifiable? Add acceptance criteria to guarantee long-term proof verification."
- Author: "Escrow signer rotation is implemented with dual-signature verification for 30 days; added tests for proof verification with rotated signer keys."
- Benji Clarke (reviewer): "Minor: prefer consistent metric names (audit_canon.*). Also please add an alert on escrow.apply-failures > 5/min for 5m."
- Author: "Addressed both comments; exported metrics and added alert rule in observability-pack/alerts/kms-escrow.yaml."
- CI: initial run failed (audit consumer timeout), rerun: pass.
- Final approval comments: Miguel: "Approved after threat-model and e2e tests added." Priya: "Approved." Benji: "LGTM."

Security review summary: SEC-112 review completed; risk note: escrow exposes additional metadata (applied_regions) that must be treated as sensitive; added redaction for non-admin views and ensured audit-canon only emits pseudonymized tenant identifiers by default. KMS providers: adapters were implemented for AWS KMS and Azure Key Vault; both adapters only return wrapped key material and never expose raw key bytes to the escrow service.

Operational runbook highlights: docs/operator/runbooks/kms-rotation-escrow.md includes: pre-checks (quota, adapter health), staged rollout (canary tenant group), revert steps (re-issue previous rotation-proof and run rollback endpoint), and alerting map.

Backward compatibility and mitigation: No consumer-facing API changes to existing GenerateKey/WrapKey endpoints. The escrow and delegation proxies are opt-in behind feature flags (rotation_escrow_enabled, delegation_proxy_enabled) so existing deployments are unaffected until the feature flags are set.

Post-merge actions:
- Coordinate with SRE to enable DB migration during low traffic window (see Linear ENG-5021).
- Schedule operator training session and post a summary to #security-compliance.
- Monitor escrow.apply-failures and canonicalizer consumer lag for first 72 hours after rollout.

Merge: squashed and merged into main on 2025-11-20 by Aisha Kapoor.

If you'd like, I can extract only the docs changes into a separate small PR for backporting to the v1.12 release branch.
